column1: The turbine bypass dumps shall be designed with dispersion headers internal to the condenser to adequately disperse the steam safely into the condenser for all possible extreme transient scenarios.

column1: An Environmental Impact Assessment Study (EIA) will be completed by Owner and copy of the same will be made available to Contractor. A Preliminary Environmental Assessment ('PEA') or Environmental and Social Impact Assessment ('E S IA') was conducted by the Offtaker and is provided in OTS Part A, Annex 3.31 of Part III (Drawings and Diagrams).

It is anticipated that the Project's development will necessitate the involvement of international lenders for financing. Given this, the Project's assessment will need to account for the requirements of international lenders in addition to the local regulations. With the specific international lenders currently unknown, the key requirements, which have been considered within this Scoping report, comprise the Equator Principles III (2013) and associated IFC Performance Standards (2012). The Project will be expected to comply with the most stringent standards should national/IFC requirements differ.

The Owner will progress the EIA Study with the intention that the Environmental Permit is available soon after the time of Contract Award. Contractor shall be responsible for providing all the necessary technical and environmental inputs to the extent required for the EIA study. After Contract Award any amendment to  the  EIA  Study  and  the  Environmental  Permit  will  be  the  responsibility  of  the  Owner  and  the  EPC Contractor.
Waste management during construction will be in accordance with the Waste Management Plan developed specifically for this project and in accordance with Government and Company approved plan.

Hazardous  Area  Classification  drawings  shall  be  developed  in  accordance  with  the  latest  revision  of ANSI/API  RP-505  and  Company  Standard  SAES-B-068  during  the  PP  Phase.  The  Area  Classification drawings shall be prepared from the project plot plans and the process schedule of hazardous materials to determine the potential sources of hazard.

All areas of the where concentrations of gas may occur due to normal leakage or process fault or ventilation system failure shall be classed as hazardous locations. The Contractor shall calculate and produce area classification drawings and documentation for the whole site area. The classified area shall be as defined within the relevant regulations and standards. All equipment within each area shall be uniquely identified and be fully compliant with the standards and regulations.",,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
